start: PBH enables verified users to execute transactions guaranteeing top of block inclusion
end: enabling a more frictionless user experience.

start: Priority Blockspace for Humans introduces a new transaction ordering policy
end: making transactions fairer for real users.

start: The World Chain Builder implements a custom block ordering policy
end: adheres to the OP Stack spec.

start: Each block has a “PBH blockspace capacity”
end: to fill the remainder of the block.

start: If the amount of pending PBH transactions exceed the PBH blockspace capacity
end: transactions within PBH blockspace are ordered by priority fee.

start: In the event that the block builder is offline
end: with standard OP Stack ordering rules.

start: Note that rollup-boost will always fallback
Upon submitting a PBH bundle to the network
end: mark the bundle for priority inclusion.

start: When a user sends a transaction to a node, the pending transaction is forwarded to the sequencer
Note that transaction ordering within the payload builder is not enforced at the protocol level.
In order to implement priority blockspace for humans, a World Chain block builder is being developed
end: included at the top of the block.
